newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VUB swings to loss due to accounting move.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VUB swings to loss due to accounting move.

text.p: Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB a.s. VSEO.BV on Friday said it sharp swing to a net loss of 1.314 billion crowns ($42.6 million) for the first nine months was mainly the result of a decision to settle its risk assets.

The bank said in a statement that the result, which compares to a 2.187 billion crown profit for the January-September period last year, that it has begun minimalising "accounting interest on arrears, which could become irredeemable claims".
The statement also said the bank had not accounted for revenue from classified loans.
VUB spokeswoman Klara Kozakova refused immediate further comment. Other bank officials were not immediately available.
The bank said it still expects to turn a profit for the whole of 1996, but lower than its 648.7 million crown net in 1995.
VUB accounts for around 60 percent of company loans in the country. It is controlled by the state through a majority stake held by the state National Property Fund, the privatisation agency.
VUB is one of the three largest Slovak banks still awaiting privatisation, which has been effectively postponed by law until the March 31, 1997.
-- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687 ($ = 30.85 Slovak Crowns)
